calls.reason: In KPMG's mid-2023 survey, 21% of large-company decision makers ranked doubts about accuracy and reliability among their top three barriers. A GPT-4 coding study found plausible but wrong code that needed expert checking. Together these support the modest 'one reason' claim.

A September 2023 paper calls hallucination an unsolved problem in language models. OpenAI itself warned against higher-risk use without verification. Retrieval-based fixes cut errors but did not remove them, so the main point that these systems are unreliable held up.

A 2020 PNAS study showed AI adversaries steering human volunteers' choices. A 2025 HBS experiment with 1,161 participants found manipulative chatbot farewells measurably increased engagement. That covers both the earlier cases and the later accumulation.

The evidence is mixed. A knee MRI study using simulated AI found AI-first teamwork beat humans or AI alone. An MIT radiology experiment found AI help did not raise average accuracy and that AI alone sometimes did better.

'Understanding' has no agreed test, and the evidence cuts both ways. The Reversal Curse paper documents transfer failures, while Webb et al. found GPT-3 matched humans on new analogy problems. Neither settles broad reliability.

Insilico's drug was still in Phase II and BenevolentAI's BEN-2293 missed its efficacy endpoints. But the packet has no full survey of AI-designed drugs, and the AI-assisted repurposing of baricitinib muddies the broader reading.
